newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-MONTGOMERY PARTNERS OLD RIVAL FOR TEST.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-MONTGOMERY PARTNERS OLD RIVAL FOR TEST.

text.p: An irony not lost on Springbok centre Percy Montgomery is that the man he partners in his debut test on Saturday -- Blue Bull Danie van Schalkwyk -- lined up against him last year when he made his first appearance in Western Province colours.

"That was the only time I've ever played against Danie, when I made my debut at provincial level for W.P. against Northerns in the centre. But he's a great guy and I think we'll work well together at Kings Park on Saturday," Montgomery told Reuters o Thursday.
Montgomery and Van Schalkwyk certainly combined well for the first time at Springbok practice on Wednesday but the pressures and nerves of a test match are another thing altogether.
"My main goal on Saturday is that I just want to give a little something extra to the side as a first cap. But a good win against the Lions is obviously the overriding aim," Montgomery said.
"It's a great honour to represent the Springboks -- to be in this team is every boy's dream. I didn't expect it this soon but, here and now, I'm really looking forward to it.
"It's definitely a must-win game on Saturday but the guys have been training hard this past week and we are pretty confident."
The 23-year-old W.P. utility back has enjoyed a meteoric rise to the green and gold, helped greatly by the recent spate of Springbok injuries as well as by his trusty left kicking boot.

South African coach Carel du Plessis, recognising Montgomery's abundant natural rugby talent, has drafted the Villagers club player into his test team in place of another goal-kicking centre -- Griqualand's injured Edrich Lubbe.
Montgomery will be the first-choice kicker for the Springboks, although du Plessis is confident that flyhalf Henry Honiball can also fulfil the role if required.
While Montgomery, who has also played at flyhalf and on the wing, has cemented his berth in the W.P. side this season at inside centre, he will play outside van Schalkwyk on Saturday.

The temptation to play the Northern Transvaal pair of van Schalkwyk and Andre Snyman as the centre combination was resisted by du Plessis who has instead switched Snyman across to the right wing for the injured James Small.
One potential advantage for Montgomery as a centre is that he has twice played against the 1997 Lions: for W.P. and for the Emerging Springboks in Wellington.

"I've been watching both Jeremy Guscott -- I played against him in the Province-Lions game -- and Scott Gibbs and I know their play. Hopefully we can just turn it round on Saturday. We'll see how it goes.

"Certainly, a major threat in this Lions side is their back line and Gibbs is a very physical player although I don't think that's the only part of his game. If we stop him and just work round him, it'll be fine."
A final bonus for Montgomery is that he will have his provincial teammate Pieter Rossouw, another test debutant on Saturday, beside him on the left wing.
"That's really great. I know the way he plays and he obviously knows how I play. Hopefully we can get a good linkage going there."
